root.name: Kangaroo Defense: Keres Defense, Transpositional Variation

overview: After 1.d4 e6 2.c4 Bb4+ 3.Nc3 the position is a Nimzo-Indian by transposition, since the usual reply is 3...Nf6, though Black can also play 3...c5. Black pins the knight, aims to double White's pawns with ...Bxc3+ and holds the centre with pieces rather than pawns. White gets the bishop pair and a big centre.

white_ideas.idea: Play e3 and Bd3 (Rubinstein) or Qc2 (Classical) to keep the bishop pair and meet ...Bxc3 with Qxc3
Build a big centre with e3 and Nge2 or f3 and e4
Gain the bishop pair and attack the doubled pawns

black_ideas.idea: Play ...Nf6 and ...Bxc3+ to double the white pawns
Control e4 with ...Nf6 and ...d5 or ...b6 and ...Bb7

typical_structures.structure: Nimzo-Indian with doubled c-pawns for White, Black bishop pair given up
Rubinstein structure with c4/d4/e3 against ...d5 and ...c5

character.notes: Reads as a Nimzo-Indian: rich but strategic, neither especially sharp nor passive.

soundness.notes: Sound; the Nimzo-Indian is a main defence.

structure.notes: Central tension, with the centre undecided for a long time: flexible.

approach.notes: This move order is a transposition to the Nimzo-Indian, a main-line defence; standard.

level.notes: Nimzo plans are understanding-heavy: doubled pawns, bishop pair and control of e4.

character.reason: A Nimzo-Indian type with rich play but no forced lines (the Rubinstein is Balanced).

soundness.reason: The Nimzo is a main defence.

approach.reason: A transposition to a main defence.

level.reason: Nimzo ideas need understanding of structure and piece play, but plans are well known.

plans.reason: The pin ...Bxc3+ doubles White's pawns for the bishop pair.
